ru: Я рабо́тал бы ме́ньше, е́сли бы мог.
note: Imperfective бы+past with an imperfective protasis; present counterfactual 'would work' is right.

ru: На э́той неде́ле я бу́ду рабо́тать до́ма.
en_alt: This week I will be working at home.
note: Compound future correctly rendered 'will be working'; до́ма also licenses 'at home'.

en_alt: What do you work as?
note: 'What do you do for work?' is natural; the instrumental construction also licenses the sibling's more literal 'What do you work as?'.

en: The working father came back late.
note: The comma-set relative 'The father, who works, came back late' reads oddly; the attributive participle is naturally an English attributive adjective.
Past active participle correctly rendered as a relative clause.

ru: Рабо́тая в Москве́, она́ вы́учила ру́сский.
note: Imperfective gerund correctly rendered 'While working'.

en_alt: They were working in the field.
note: Imperfective past also supports the progressive reading.

ru: Я ра́довалась бы бо́льше без забо́т.
en: I would be happier without worries.
note: 'Gladder' is not idiomatic English as a comparative here.
The imperfective durative 'was glad about' is correct; the frame collision should be fixed on the perfective partner обра́доваться ('Mum was delighted at the good news'), not here.

en: The children will be rejoicing at the first snow.
note: Three 'will be glad' collisions with обра́доваться, one of them near-identical ('Soon the children will be glad of the holidays'); the compound future бу́дут+infinitive is durative, and 'will be rejoicing at' commits to it where 'will be being glad' is impossible.

ru: Я разбира́лся бы в э́том, е́сли бы учи́лся.

en_alt: Do you know much about music?
note: разбира́ться в also renders as 'know a lot about'; alt keeps the word-bank from rejecting it.

en_alt: I know a lot about music.
He knows a lot about cars.

ru: Ско́ро я бу́ду разбира́ться в програ́ммах лу́чше.
note: Compound future left as bare 'will understand' deliberately — 'will be understanding' is not English for a stative verb.
Imperfective past correctly progressive.

ru: Я разбуди́л бы тебя́ ра́ньше, но ты уста́л.
note: The coordinate clause «но ты уста́л» reads as the present state 'but you are tired', which fixes this as a present counterfactual — 'would wake', not 'would have woken'.

en_alt: Will you wake the child up?

ru: Я разбужу́ тебя́ за́втра в семь.
en_alt: I will wake you up tomorrow at seven.

note: The translation is right, but the headword gloss 'to unfold' does not cover the 'turn (a vehicle) around' or 'unwrap' senses this word's examples use; the gloss may be the half that needs widening.
Correct sense; see the gloss-mismatch flag on the ты sibling.
No protasis and no collision, so the present counterfactual 'would unwrap' stands.

ru: Я сейча́с разверну́ ка́рту на столе́.
en_alt: I will now unfold the map on the table.

ru: Я развела́ бы костёр, но нет дров.
note: Translation correct (развести́ костёр = light a fire) and the present coordinate clause «но нет дров» rightly fixes it as a present counterfactual; but the headword gloss 'to breed' covers none of the light-a-fire / dilute senses its own examples use.

ru: Мы разведём кур на фе́рме ско́ро.
note: Sentence-final «ско́ро» is slightly marked in Russian but not wrong; not worth a reorder that would retarget any inflect index.

en_alt: The city is developing quickly.
note: бы́стро is glossed 'quickly' corpus-wide.

ru: Нау́ка развива́лась бы быстре́е без войн.

en_alt: Children develop differently.

note: Compound future correctly rendered 'will be developing'.

en_alt: We spent a long time solving this mystery.
note: 'Working out' is a fine rendering of the imperfective; the alt keeps the headword gloss 'solve' available.
Habitual imperfective correctly a simple present.

ru: В бино́кль я разгляжу́ да́льний бе́рег.
en_alt: Through the binoculars I will make out the far shore.

ru: Я не могу́ разгляде́ть но́мер до́ма.

en_alt: She will make out a swallow in the sky.

ru: Я разгляде́ла бы но́мер при све́те.
note: No past protasis and no collision, so the perfective reads as a future-referring counterfactual single event.

ru: В музе́е я бу́ду разгля́дывать ка́ждую карти́ну.
note: Compound future correctly rendered 'will be examining'.

en_alt: He was examining the map for a long time.
note: The imperfective past also carries the progressive reading, which the perfective partner could not.

ru: Он разгля́дывал бы ка́рту до́льше без спе́шки.
en_alt: He would examine the map for longer without the rush.
note: 'For longer' is the more idiomatic en_gb comparative; alt rather than a rewrite since the existing form is acceptable.

ru: По доро́ге домо́й мы бу́дем разгова́ривать о пое́здке.
en: On the way home, we will be talking about the trip.
note: бу́дем+infinitive is the imperfective compound future and should read 'will be talking', not a bare 'will talk' that a perfective could also carry.

ru: Мы разгова́ривали бы ча́ще, е́сли бы не рабо́та.

en_alt: They were talking all night.
I am talking to the neighbour.

note: 'Rang out' is the idiomatic English for разда́ться and commits to the perfective single event.

en_alt: Footsteps rang out in the corridor.

ru: В тишине́ разда́лся бы любо́й шо́рох.
en: In the silence any rustle would ring out.
note: 'Any rustle would sound' is not natural English with an intransitive 'sound'; 'ring out' is the standard rendering of разда́ться and keeps the perfective single-event reading.
The 'get' frame collision is with a perfective imperative ('Get undressed and lie down'); a habitual declarative against a command leaves plenty of cue, so no change is warranted.

ru: Она́ разде́лась и вста́ла под душ.
Е́сли бы бы́ло жа́рко, я разде́лась бы.
note: Past protasis plus perfective apodosis correctly gives the past counterfactual 'would have got undressed / had been hot'.
Imperative is unambiguous against the imperfective partner's habitual present.

ru: Де́ти разде́лись и пры́гнули в бассе́йн.
Он бы разобра́л мото́р, е́сли бы уме́л.
note: Imperfective stative protasis (уме́л) makes this a present counterfactual, so 'would take apart' is right.

en_alt: They took the tent down.
Tomorrow I will take the old wardrobe apart.
Will you take the tent down?
He took the old clock apart.
I will take this mechanism apart.

ru: Я разобра́лся бы в э́том сам.

en_alt: Tomorrow I will sort out the documents.
I will sort this problem out.

ru: По́сле конце́рта мы разойдёмся по дома́м.
en_alt: After the concert we will go our separate ways home.
note: разойти́сь по дома́м is the set phrase; the existing 'part and go home' is fine, the alt gives the idiomatic reading.

en_alt: Will you go your separate ways late?
note: 'Will you part late?' is stilted but consistent with the headword gloss; the alt gives natural English without losing the reciprocal sense.

ru: Го́сти разошли́сь бы ра́ньше без му́зыки.
en_alt: The guests would have left earlier without the music.
note: Perfective бы+past also supports the past counterfactual; kept 'would part' as en_gb since no collision forces the change.

en_alt: The guests left late.

ru: Роди́тели разреша́ли бы бо́льше, е́сли бы доверя́ли.
note: The imperfective habitual 'would allow' is correct; the 'would allow' collision belongs to the perfective partner «Я разреши́ла бы тебе́ оста́ться», which I retranslate instead.

en_alt: The parents allow him to play.
note: Frame collision is only with a perfective imperative ('Allow me to come in'), which stays distinguishable.

ru: С ле́та нам бу́дут разреша́ть купа́ться здесь.
note: Compound future correctly rendered 'will be allowing'.

ru: Они́ не разреша́ли кури́ть в до́ме.
en_alt: They used not to allow smoking in the house.
note: Imperfective past also carries the habitual reading the perfective partner cannot.
Translation is right (разреши́ть спор = settle/resolve a dispute) but the headword gloss 'to allow' does not cover the resolve sense two of its examples use; the gloss is likely the half to widen.
Correct sense; see the gloss-mismatch flag on the sibling.

ru: За́втра дире́ктор разреши́т нам уйти́ ра́ньше.

en: I would have allowed you to stay.
note: Collides on 'would allow' with the imperfective partner's habitual counterfactual; with no protasis the perfective бы+past is the past counterfactual single event, so 'would have allowed' fixes the wrong side and leaves the imperfective as the only 'would allow'.
Impersonal plural correctly rendered as an English passive.
раскры́ть преступле́ние is the set collocation 'solve a crime'; a literal 'reveal' would be wrong here.

ru: Он бы раскры́л пра́вду, е́сли бы не боя́лся.
note: Imperfective stative protasis 'if he were not afraid' fixes this as a present counterfactual.

ru: Ско́ро я раскро́ю тебе́ свой план.

en_alt: I will fling open the doors for the guests.

ru: Она́ бы распахну́ла две́ри для госте́й.
en_alt: She would fling the doors open for the guests.

ru: Я расскажу́ тебе́ всю исто́рию за́втра.
en_alt: Tomorrow I will tell you the whole story.

ru: Он рассказа́л нам о свое́й пое́здке.
Он бы рассказа́л пра́вду, е́сли бы спроси́ли.
en: He would have told the truth if he had been asked.
note: Collides on 'would tell' with the imperfective partner; «е́сли бы спроси́ли» is a perfective past protasis, so the past counterfactual is the reading this side actually carries.

ru: Он расска́зывал бы о войне́ ре́же, е́сли бы мог забы́ть.
en: He would tell stories about the war less often if he could forget.
note: 'Tell about the war' is not idiomatic en_gb; the sibling «Он ча́сто расска́зывал о войне́» already uses 'told stories about', and this also clears the 'would tell' frame collision from the other side.

ru: Ве́чером я бу́ду расска́зывать де́тям ска́зку.
en_alt: In the evening I will be telling the children a fairy tale.
note: Compound future correctly 'will be telling'; ска́зка is glossed 'fairy tale' corpus-wide.

en_alt: He often used to talk about the war.
note: Habitual imperfective past also supports 'used to'.

en_alt: Do you tell the children fairy tales?
Grandmother tells the children fairy tales.
